# EEZ Quickstarts

> Fifteen interactive walkthroughs of the Ethereum Economic Zone, each built on real
> protocol source cited at a pinned commit rather than on pseudocode. Covers writing
> contracts that call across rollups, running the stack, and how Rollup0 settles and proves.

Every code panel on this site is rendered from JavaScript at runtime, so fetching a page
gives you the shell and not the content. These files hand over the content directly: each
walkthrough's narration and code, the full compilable Solidity behind the Solidity ones,
and the runnable Foundry tests.

Two things worth knowing before you use any of it. EEZ is pre-mainnet, so treat
capability claims as design intent rather than shipped behaviour; the proof system in the
public source is dev-grade ECDSA, not production ZK. And every citation here is pinned to
a commit SHA, so a link tells you exactly which revision a claim was true of.

## Dapp developers

Writing contracts that call across rollups.

- [How to get your contract's address on another rollup](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q7-your-cross-chain-address.html): Learn how to read it, or deploy it.
- [How to call a contract on another rollup](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q2-send-a-cross-chain-call.html): Learn how to encode it like any normal call and send it to the proxy.
- [How to handle msg.sender across chains](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q3-fix-the-msg-sender-gotcha.html): Learn how to whitelist the proxy instead of the address you expected.
- [How to check an address is a real proxy](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q4-check-if-an-address-is-a-proxy.html): Learn how to read the on-chain registry instead of guessing.
- [How the guard makes sure only proxy calls reach execution](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q6-why-you-cant-call-the-manager-directly.html): Learn how UnauthorizedProxy() stops any call that isn't proxy-routed.
- [How to encode a call's content hash](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/dapp-developers/q5-encode-a-calls-content-hash.html): Learn how to hash eight fields in the one order that works.

## Rollup operators

Standing the stack up and driving it.

- [How to run the whole stack locally](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro1-run-the-devnet-with-kurtosis.html): Learn how to bring up the node, proof-signer and the L1 in a disposable network.
- [How to deploy the protocol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro2-deploy-the-protocol.html): Learn how one command deploys EEZ, the proof system and your manager.
- [How to run against a real testnet](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro3-run-a-real-chiado-l2.html): Learn how to point the same stack at Chiado instead of a sandbox.
- [How to send and test a cross-chain call](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/rollup-operators/ro4-send-and-test-cross-chain-calls.html): Learn how to drive both fronts and read real pass/fail numbers.

## Protocol researchers

How Rollup0 actually settles and proves.

- [How the four components divide the work](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr1-the-four-components-of-rollup0.html): Learn how sequencer, composer, proof-signer and deriver each fit.
- [How L1 stays the source of truth](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr2-commit-first-repair-if-needed.html): Learn how an L2 commits first and L1 then settles or repairs it.
- [How the composer proves a batch](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr4-how-the-composer-proves-a-batch.html): Learn how one gRPC stream carries header, blocks and a signature.
- [How the deriver rebuilds L2 from L1](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr3-the-deriver.html): Learn how the whole chain is reconstructed from L1 data alone.
- [How the address is derived](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/protocol-researchers/pr5-how-the-address-is-derived.html): Learn how two values become a salt and a CREATE2 address.

## Compilable source

Real files, not fragments: pragma, imports and a contract wrapper, all building under solc 0.8.28. Each mirrors the upstream function its walkthrough cites.

- [snippets/q7-create-proxy.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q7-create-proxy.sol): full source behind How to get your contract's address on another rollup
- [snippets/q2-cross-chain-call.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q2-cross-chain-call.sol): full source behind How to call a contract on another rollup
- [snippets/q3-msg-sender.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q3-msg-sender.sol): full source behind How to handle msg.sender across chains
- [snippets/q4-proxy-registry.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q4-proxy-registry.sol): full source behind How to check an address is a real proxy
- [snippets/q6-manager-direct.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q6-manager-direct.sol): full source behind How the guard makes sure only proxy calls reach execution
- [snippets/q5-content-hash.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q5-content-hash.sol): full source behind How to encode a call's content hash
- [snippets/q1-compute-address.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/q1-compute-address.sol): full source behind How the address is derived

## Runnable tests

Foundry tests with no forge-std and no submodules, so they drop into an existing suite. `cd snippets && forge test`.

- [snippets/test/Q3MsgSender.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q3MsgSender.t.sol): proves the behaviour in How to handle msg.sender across chains
- [snippets/test/Q6ManagerDirect.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q6ManagerDirect.t.sol): proves the behaviour in How the guard makes sure only proxy calls reach execution
- [snippets/test/Q5ContentHash.t.sol](https://0xarmagan.github.io/eez-demos/snippets/test/Q5ContentHash.t.sol): proves the behaviour in How to encode a call's content hash
